newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Analysts favour Elbit defence spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Analysts favour Elbit defence spin-off.

text.p: As the wide-ranging businesses of Israel's Elbit Ltd go their separate ways this week, analysts are most enthusiastic about the defence-electronics business, Elbit Systems Ltd.
"They seemed to have developed a global niche in the upgrade of fighter aircraft, which is a very, very big business," said Keith Phillips of Societe General Strauss Turnbull in London.
Elbit Systems and Elbit Medical Imaging Ltd, once divisions of Elbit Ltd, began trading as independent companies on Nasdaq on Wednesday and on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Thursday.
Elbit Ltd will retain a grab-bag of electronics business ranging from television manufacturing to industrial electronics.

Elbit Systems soared nearly 210 percent in very active trading its first day in Tel Aviv, following a similar performance on the Nasdaq a day earlier, while Elbit Medical plunged 42 percent and Elbit Ltd dropped 10 percent.
But analysts said the initial reaction did not reflect the market's long-term view of the three companies.
Phillips said Elbit had been broken up on a net asset value basis, rather than an earnings basis, which is how the market values operating companies like the three Elbit successors.

For now, there are only "very rough valuations" based on earnings projections for Elbit Systems and none at all for the others, said Arnon Rubinstein of BZW in London. He predicted trading will remain volatile in all three shares next week.

Although the outlooks for each of the three companies vary considerably, analysts cheered the break-up as a way of letting the market properly value Elbit's many businesses. Rubinstein said management should have better control over the individual businesses.
He said the biggest beneficiary should be Elbit Systems. As a pure defence-electronics play, the company will be freer to join in the merger and acquisitions wave underway in defence.

Phillips noted that because of the decline in world defence spending, many air forces were saving money by upgrading their aging fighter jets rather than replacing them. "It's a booming business and (Elbit's) leading the world," he said.

Elbit Medical Imaging, which makes ultrasound and other medical equiopment, will benefit less as a stand-alone, analysts said. "There seems to be some margin pressure," said Phillips. "It's not a bad business, but it's not as exciting as the military."

Rubinstein said Elbit Ltd was tantamount to a start-up. It has already sold all or part of two of the businesses that were supposed to belong to the company and analysts say the television manufacturing operation is being pared back and may be closed altogether.

That leaves Elbit Ltd with its holding in Elbit Vision Systems, which makes automatic pattern recognition systems, and 20 percent of Inframetrics, which develops products based on infrared technology.
Rubinstein said Elbit Ltd has about $50 million in real estate and cash as well as experienced management. "You trust the management to develop new businesses," he said. "It's a good start-up."
